 Judgment
This claim petition is filed under section 163-A of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioner that on 12.11.2018 at about 9.00 a.m. when he was driving the Maruthi Celerio car bearing Reg.
No.KA-02-MN-5248 towards Gulur, at that time, the rider of the Bullet bike bearing Reg.
No.KA-40-X-1535 who was proceeding to Mallasandra, hit the front portion of the Maruthi Celerio Car.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained injuries.

Immediately, after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Bagepalli wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Navachethana Hospital, Yelahanka New town, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment for his accidental injuries as an inpatient from 12.11.2018 to 16.11.2018 and underwent surgery of right wrist joint and right radial styloid displacement.

Later due to swelling on the right wrist, the petitioner has been taking physiotherapy treatment at Madhu Ortho and Trauma Center,
Dasarahalli, Bengaluru.

entities.text:
Madhu Ortho and Trauma Center,
Dasarahalli
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is stated that he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges.
Due to the accidental injuries the petitioner is unable to do his work as he was doing earlier.

3. It is further submitted that the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working in General Stores and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month and contributing his entire income to the family and the petitioner is the sole bread winner to his family.
It is further submitted that, the accident occurred between the car and Bullet bike, inspite of due diligence and care taken by the petitioner while driving the car the accident was occurred.
The jurisdictional police have also registered the case in crime No.323/2018 for an offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC of Bagepalli Police.

The respondent No.1 is the RC owner of Bullet bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-X-1535 and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of Maruthi Celerio Car have accepted premium towards personal accident cover, both are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence prayed to award compensation to the tune of Rs.5,00,000/- together with cost and interest.

2
4. On service of notice, both respondents appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed their written statements.

5. The respondent No.1 in his objection has denied the entire averments of the petition filed against him and contended that he is the owner of the offending Motor cycle and also admits that as on the date of accident, the motorcycle was being driven by him and the said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of car in a zig zag manner and caused the accident.
Since the alleged accident occurred due to the negligent act of the petitioner himself, the respondent No.1 has lodged a complaint against the petitioner with the jurisdictional police.
He further contended that the petitioner has sustained only simple injuries and he has not taken any treatment as inpatient.

As per Sec.163A, the petition is maintainable only where the petitioner has sustained permanent disability whereas, as per the charge sheet there is no such permanent disability or injuries sustained by the petitioner.
On all other grounds, prays to dismiss the petition.

6. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petitioner is the RC owner of Maruthi Celerio Car and 2 nd respondent had issued private car package policy in respect of the petitioner's vehicle.

In the present petition, the owner of the third party vehicle is made as a respondent No.1 and the petitioner's insurer is arrayed as the 2 nd respondent whereas there is no privity of contract between the 1st and 2nd respondent as an insured and the insurer.
Thus, the petition is bad for misjoinder of parties.
Further it contended that 2nd respondent has not issued any policy in respect of the 1st respondent's vehicle.
On other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

7. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor-in-office has has framed following issues:-:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner proves that on 12.11.2018 at about 9.00 a.m., while he was proceeding in a Maruthi Celerio car bearing Reg.

No.KA-02-MN-5248, near Chennarayanapalli Cross, Gulur road, Bagepalli Taluk, at that time, the rider of the Bullet bike bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-X-1535 by riding the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner, caused the accident, due to which he sustained injuries?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ? If so, from whom and how much?
3. What Order or award?
8. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to 11 were marked on his behalf.
On the other hand, respondents have not led any evidence before the court.

9. Heard arguments.
10.

My answers to the above Issues are as follows:-
T.V. Amarnath vs M.B. Rameshkumar on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163724693/
3  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following :
 REASONS 11.
Issue No.1 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with relief to grant a compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in RTA.
12. It is important to note that, at the first instance the petitioner filed this petition u/s. 163A of MV Act, therefore, question of considering rash and negligence does not arise.
What the petitioner has to establish is that, there was an accident between two vehicles and in the said accident the petitioner sustained injuries.

Therefore petitioner need not prove that, the accident in question took place only due to rash and negligent of riding of the rider of Bullet bike bearing Reg.No.KA-40-X-1535 involved in the accident.

However petitioner has to prove that he sustained injuries in the very accident, due to involvement of his Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MN-5248.
13.

At the out set, it is pertinent to note that petition filed U/sec.163A, the question to be considered by the tribunal is that the involvement of the vehicles against which the compensation is sought for and not whether there is rash or negligence on part of the rider/drivers of the both vehicle against which the compensation is claimed.
The aspect of negligence has no rule whatsoever to decide the question of the entitlement for compensation.

In the decision reported in ILR 2008 KAR 1249 rendered in the case of Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs Salma and others

Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd., Vs Salma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2004) 5 SCC 385 rendered in the case of Deepal Girishbhai Sono and others V/S United India Insurance Co. Ltd., it is held that;
"Section 163-A also covers the cases where negligence is even on part of the victim held excluding the defense of contributory negligence".

entities.text: Deepal Girishbhai Sono and others V/S United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd Vs Sunil Kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In a proceedings under section 163-A of IMV Act it is not open for the insurer to raise any defence of negligence on part of the victim."

17. The pith and substance of these decisions is that, section 163-A(2) of the Act, does not specifically exclude a possible defence of the insurer based on negligence of the claimant as contemplated by section 140(4) to permit such defence to be introduced the insurer and/or to understand the provisions of section 163(A) of the Act to be contemplating an such situation would go contrary to the very legislative object behind introduction of section 163(A) of the Act, namely,
final compensation within a limited time frame on the basis of the structured formula to over come situations where the claims of compensation on the basis of fault liability was taking an unduly long time.

On a coalesce of the afore-quoted legal fresco and on the bedrock of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and Hon'ble Apex Court the having regard to the crux of the dispute between the parties, the above principles are squarely applicable to the case on hand.
For the said reasons, in a proceeding under section 163-A of the Act it is not open for the insurer to raise any defence of negligence on the part of the victim.

18. In the present case, though the FIR registered against the petitioner who is the driver of the Maruthi Clerio Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MN-5248 in Crime No.323/2018 of Bagepalli P.S.
Chickballapura.

After thorough investigation, the police have submitted charge sheet against petitioner as per Ex.P.2 for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
19.
As per Section 163A and 164 of the Act, rash and negligence need not be proved, the petitioner has to be prove only involvement of the vehicle.

So, as per the recent decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, we have to grant the compensation under section 163-A of the Act on the basis of structured formula is in the nature of the final award and the adjudication there under is required to be made without an requirement of any proof of negligence of the driver/owner of the vehicle/s involved in the accident and under section 163-A of the Act.

20. In view of above provisions of law and case laws, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under section 163-A of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the tribunal.
Admittedly the respondents have not challenged the oral and documentary evidence led by the claimant.
The version of the petitioner remained unchallenged and undisputed.
Infact respondents have not chosen to appear before the court and contest the matter.
Hence an adverse inference can be drawn against the respondents U/Sec.114(g) of Indian Evidence Act.
21. This Tribunal has carefully gone through the evidence placed by petitioner.
It is important to note that, the present petition is filed under 163-A of M.V.Act.
It is also important to note that if a petition is filed under 163(A) of M.V. Act, seeking award of compensation due to injuries sustained by him in the said accident.
It is also not disputed that, motorcycle bearing reg.No. KA-40-X-1535 is also involved in the accident.
It is not in dispute that the very collusion took place between two vehicles.
In my view when once it is demonstrated that, in the very accident two vehicles were involved, which itself is sufficient to invoke the provisions U/Sec.163(A) of Motor Vehicle Act.

T.V. Amarnath vs M.B. Rameshkumar on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163724693/
5 22.
Petitioner filed petition under section 163-A of MV Act.
Hence in view of the above decisions, it is observed that claimant is entitled to compensation without proving negligence.
The Discharge summary produced by the petitioner by filing a memo clearly disclose that, the petitioner has sustained injuries in the above accident and he had taken treatment in the Hospital.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW-1 coupled with the documents produced as per Ex.P1 to 11 this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident was occurred by the involvement of the Bullet motorcycle bearing Reg.No. KA-40-X-1535 and Maruthi Clerio Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MN-5248 and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the petitioner.
By the oral and documentary evidence petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to the involvement of both vehicles.
Hence, this Tribunal need not discuss much about this Issue.
With this observation Issue No.1 is answered 'In the Affirmative'.
23. Issue NO.2 : It is proved the involvement of vehicles in the accident under Issue No.1.
The respondents have not appeared before the court to refute the contention of the petitioner.

Therefore,
under these circumstances, petitioner being injured is entitled for compensation.
24. The contentions of the petitioner that he was working in General stores and earning income of Rs.15,000/- per month as per column No.6 of the petition after amendment.
But the petitioner has not produced any documents with respect that income and avocation.

Further PW.1 got exhibited wound certificate and also produced discharge summary along with Memo which disclose that, the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Pain and tenderness immobility over the right wrist joint X-ray of right wrist joint shows Radial styloid displacement.
As per the discharge summary of Mahachethana Hospital, Bengaluru, the following procedure was done i.e., closed reduction and K-wire fixation pop cast application and GA on 13.11.2018.
PW-1 has stated that due to accidental injuries, he is not in a position to attend his regular work till today and lost his earnings.
25. The petitioner has not given evidence with respect to disability.
Therefore, there is no doctor evidence to physical disability of the petitioner due to the accidental injury.
However, the discharge summary as well as case sheet discloses the injury and treatment.
Therefore, it is proved that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the above said accident and involvement of Bullet bike and Maruthi Clerio Car.

It is pertinent to note that, on perusal of Ex.P6 Insurance policy issued in respect of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MN-5248 it reflects that, in Limit of Liability Clause it is mentioned as follows:
Limit of Liability: Under Section ii-1(i) of the policy - Death of bodily injury - Such amount as is necessary to meet there requirements of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Under Section II - 1(ii) of the policy - damage to Third Property-Rs.7.5 lakhs - (as per IMT 20) in respect of any one claim or series of claims arising out for one event.
Cover for owner-Driver under section III(CSI) Rs.200000 deductible under section T.V. Amarnath vs M.B. Rameshkumar on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163724693/
6 -1: Rs.1,000(Compulsory Deductible Rs.1000 imposed deductible Rs.0 and voluntary deductible Rs.0) and the owner/petitioner has paid an amount of Rs.100/- towards compulsory PA cover premium.

26. Hence, respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MN-5248 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner since he has collected premium for personal accident to an extent of Rs.2,00,000/-.

27. In the instant case as the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries, so as per the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, the Section.164 of MV Act says that the payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt etc., (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs of the victim, as the case may be.

28. In the instant case as the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries, and wound certificate marked at Ex.P4 and the discharge summary produced through memo discloses the petitioner has sustained fracture BB 1/3rd right forearm in the accident and he has taken treatment from 12.11.2018 to 13.11.2018 for a period of 2 days, so, as per Section.163(A) of the Motor Vehicles Amendment) Act, the petitioner is entitled for compensation amount.
As per the said section the injured person is entitled Rs.1,50,000/- including medical bill of Rs.86,082/-.
Hence, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- to the petitioner.
29. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

The 2nd respondent is stated to be the insurer of the petitioner's car, Insurance policy issued in respect of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MN-5248 it reflects that, in Limit of Liability Clause it is mentioned as follows:
Limit of Liability: Under Section ii-1(i) of the policy - Death of bodily injury - Such amount as is necessary to meet there requirements of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Under Section II -1(ii) of the policy - damage to Third Property- Rs.7.5 lakhs - (as per IMT 20) in respect of any one claim or series of claims arising out for one event.

Cover for owner-Driver under section III(CSI) Rs.200000 deductible under section -1: Rs.1,000(Compulsory Deductible Rs.1000 imposed deductible Rs.0 and voluntary deductible Rs.0) and the owner/petitioner has paid an amount of Rs.100/- towards compulsory PA cover premium.
Hence, 2nd respondent being insurer of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MN-5248 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner awarded by this tribunal.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

7 30.
Issue NO.3 :

In view of the findings given on Issues No.1 and 2 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed under Section163-A of the M.V. Act, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms:

It is hereby ordered that the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the petitioner a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Entire award amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
